Entity Structures

Legacy Platform Holdings LLC

Purpose: The main holding company that oversees all subsidiaries. It manages overall strategy, financing, and compliance for the entire Legacy Platform.

Subsidiaries:

1. Legacy Restore LLC

  • Purpose: Focuses on credit restoration and related services.

  • Products: Legacy Restore Service, Affiliate Services, Community Education, White Label Smart Credit, DIY Software, Tradelines Services.

2. Legacy Capital Solutions LLC

  • Purpose: Provides business and personal funding solutions.

  • Products: Business Credit Builder, Business & Personal Funding Service.

3. Legacy Success Coaching LLC

  • Purpose: Comprehensive coaching programs focused on both personal and business success, encompassing the four pillars.

  • Products: Financial Performance Accelerator, Business Coaching, Personal Development Coaching.

4. Legacy Knowledge Community LLC

  • Purpose: Community and educational platform for members.

  • Products: Membership Programs, Weekly Members Mastermind, Virtual and Physical Workshops, Affiliate Products (Personal Credit Building, Business, Performance, Credit Repair).

5. Legacy Integrated Consulting LLC

  • Purpose: Comprehensive consulting services across various domains, integrating different aspects of business and personal development.

  • Products: Business Strategy, Operational Consulting, Tailored Consulting Services.

6. Legacy Events LLC

  • Purpose: Event management for community engagement and education, aligning with the four pillars.

  • Products: Physical Fitness Events, Weekly Members Mastermind, Physical Workshops, Virtual Workshops.

7. Legacy Gear Collective LLC

  • Purpose: Manages physical clothing business and merchandise, creating a community around branded gear and athletic products.

  • Products: Branded Gear, Athletic Gear (Legacy Athletics), Merchandise, Amazon Affiliate Products for Starter Pack.

For a comprehensive overview that includes all aspects of your business, focusing on the executive team, operational teams, and the essential roles within those teams, here's a structured outline. This format should align well with organization in Notion and provide a clear picture of the entire organizational structure, including direct reporting lines and detailed tasks for each role.

Executive Team

  • **CEO (Founder)**Responsibilities: Sets company vision, oversees executive team, fiscal health, strategic partnerships.

  • **COO (Chief Operating Officer)**Responsibilities: Manages daily operations, oversees integration of services, operational efficiency.

    • **Direct Reports:**Operations and Logistics Manager

  • Customer Service Manager

  • **CMO (Chief Marketing Officer)**Responsibilities: Develops marketing strategy, oversees brand and membership growth.

  • **Direct Reports:**Marketing and Social Media Coordinator

  • **CCO (Chief Community Officer)**Responsibilities: Leads community engagement, content strategy on Circle.so.

  • **Direct Reports:**Events and Webinars Coordinator

  • **CTO (Chief Technology Officer)**Responsibilities: Directs technical strategy, platform integration and security.

  • **Direct Reports:**Technical Support Specialist

Operational Teams

Operations and Logistics

  • Operations and Logistics ManagerResponsibilities: Manages physical product logistics, event coordination, inventory, supplier relations.

    • **Direct Reports:**Logistics Coordinator

  • Inventory Specialist

Customer Service

  • Customer Service ManagerResponsibilities: Implements and oversees customer support operations, manages team, ensures customer satisfaction.

  • **Direct Reports:**Customer Support Representatives

Marketing and Community Engagement

  • Marketing and Social Media CoordinatorResponsibilities: Executes marketing campaigns, manages social media, enhances brand visibility.

  • Events and Webinars CoordinatorResponsibilities: Plans and executes all member and non-member events, coordinates webinar logistics.

Technical Support

  • Technical Support SpecialistResponsibilities: Manages technical inquiries, platform issues, supports integration and automation efforts.

Financial Team

  • Chief Financial Officer (CFO): While the COO can initially oversee financial matters, a dedicated CFO becomes crucial as your business grows. They would manage financial planning, risk assessment, budgeting, and ensure compliance with financial regulations.

    • Responsibilities: Oversee financial operations, develop financial strategies, manage investor relations, and ensure the profitability and financial health of the business.

    • Accountant / Bookkeeper:Responsibilities: Manage day-to-day financial transactions, payroll, invoicing, and financial reporting.

Human Resources

  • HR Manager: As your team grows, managing hiring, onboarding, employee satisfaction, and compliance with labor laws becomes a full-time job.

    • Responsibilities: Oversee recruitment processes, employee relations, benefits management, and organizational development.

Product Development Team (for Physical Products)

  • Product Manager: If your clothing line or any physical product offerings expand, having a product manager to oversee product development, market research, and lifecycle management could be beneficial.

    • Responsibilities: Conduct market research, oversee product design and development, manage production timelines, and coordinate with marketing for product launches.

Content Creation Team

  • Content Strategist / Manager: Enhances your marketing and community engagement efforts with high-quality, consistent content across all platforms.

    • Responsibilities: Develop and implement content strategy, oversee content creation (blogs, social media posts, email newsletters), and measure content performance.

Legal Counsel

  • In-House Legal Advisor or Counsel: As your business expands, especially with diverse offerings like events, consulting, and physical products, legal complexities can increase. A legal advisor can manage compliance, intellectual property, contracts, and any legal disputes.

    • Responsibilities: Oversee compliance with laws and regulations, manage contracts and agreements, protect the company's intellectual property, and provide legal advice.

IT / Security Specialist

  • IT Security Specialist: With the importance of online transactions and data security, having a role focused on cybersecurity measures is crucial.

    • Responsibilities: Implement and monitor security protocols for customer data protection, manage IT security systems, and respond to security breaches.

Community Management

  • Community Manager(s): As your community grows, especially beyond 10,000 members, having additional community managers to maintain engagement, moderate discussions, and organize community-driven events will be crucial for sustaining a vibrant community environment.

    • Responsibilities: Engage with the community, manage forums and discussion groups, organize virtual meet-ups, and gather community feedback for continuous improvement.

Integrating these roles into your organizational structure as your business grows will ensure comprehensive coverage across all functional areas, supporting your scalability and enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of your operations.

Legacy Platform Overview

  1. Legacy Building Focus: The core mission of the platform is to assist users in creating lasting legacies. This involves not just financial wealth, but also personal development, community building, and creating a positive impact that endures across generations.

  2. Pillars of the Platform: The platform is structured around key pillars - Education, Community, Wellness, Technology, and Entrepreneurship. Each pillar plays a crucial role in guiding users through their legacy-building journey.

  3. Education: Offers comprehensive learning resources, including courses and workshops on financial literacy, business intelligence, international investments, homesteading, and more. It's designed to cater to a global audience with a wide range of interests and needs.

  4. Community: Fosters a supportive environment where users can connect, share experiences, and collaborate. This includes forums, networking events, and mentorship opportunities.

  5. Wellness: Focuses on personal development and high-performance living, covering areas like mental health, physical fitness, and lifestyle choices that contribute to overall well-being.

  6. Technology: The platform leverages advanced technology, including AI, to personalize user experiences, streamline learning, and offer efficient tools for managing finances and business operations.

  7. Entrepreneurship: Encourages and supports entrepreneurial ventures, offering resources for business planning, funding, and growth strategies.

  8. Products and Services: The platform offers a range of products and services aligned with its mission. This includes Legacy Academy (educational content), Legacy Community (networking and mentorship), and Legacy Athletics (high-performance apparel). Each product is designed to integrate seamlessly with the platform's ecosystem.

  9. Global Reach and Inclusivity: The platform is designed to be globally accessible, with content and resources tailored to different demographics, including youth programs, business development tools for entrepreneurs, and lifestyle content for individuals seeking a nomadic lifestyle.

  10. Branding and Positioning: The platform is positioned as a leader in legacy building, with a strong emphasis on creating generational wealth and positive societal impact. The branding is centered around the concept of "Legacy," signifying the long-term, impactful nature of the platform's mission.

  11. Future Expansion: Plans for expanding the platform include integrating more advanced AI features, expanding the range of educational topics, and growing the community to include a more diverse global audience.

In summary, Legacy AI is a multifaceted platform designed to guide and support individuals and businesses in building lasting legacies through education, community engagement, personal wellness, and technological innovation. It's a platform that goes beyond financial success to encompass all aspects of creating a meaningful and enduring impact.

Wealth Warriors is a strong and compelling name for your financial literacy company. It evokes the feeling of joining a group of fierce warriors focused on building and managing wealth. The name highlights the company's commitment to empowering people with financial knowledge and tools, while also making it clear that you are in the business of fighting for your clients' financial success. This name effectively conveys your goal of integrating technology with finances to create a better wealth-building experience for individuals and businesses alike.

Wealth Warriors is a cutting-edge financial literacy company dedicated to empowering individuals and businesses with the knowledge and tools necessary to achieve financial success. Our team of seasoned finance experts, software engineers, and passionate educators work together to create a comprehensive suite of services tailored to the unique needs of our clients. From financial education courses and state-of-the-art software solutions to personalized consultations on taxes, life insurance, and other financial products, we strive to provide a seamless, technology-driven experience designed to help people grow and manage their wealth effectively.

At Wealth Warriors, we pride ourselves on our diverse and talented team, which consists of professionals with a wide range of expertise, including certified financial planners, tax advisors, insurance specialists, and technology innovators. Our shared goal is to bring financial education to the global market, breaking down barriers and fostering financial growth for people of all backgrounds and income levels.

When you join Wealth Warriors, you become part of an elite group of individuals who are committed to achieving financial freedom and creating a lasting legacy. Our company stands as a beacon of hope and inspiration, providing the tools and guidance necessary to overcome financial challenges and emerge victorious in the battle for wealth and prosperity.

A content plan for your Wealth Warriors YouTube channel will ensure that you effectively promote the various services and products your company offers. By creating diverse, engaging, and informative content, you can reach a wider audience and showcase the full range of your company's expertise. Here's a suggested content plan:

  1. Introduction to Wealth Warriors: Start with an introductory video that provides an overview of your company, its mission, the services and products it offers, and the types of people involved in the organization.

  2. Financial Education Series: Create a playlist of videos covering various aspects of financial literacy, such as budgeting, saving, investing, credit management, and retirement planning. Each video should be clear, concise, and engaging, with a call-to-action encouraging viewers to visit your website for more in-depth resources.

  3. Software Solutions Showcase: Produce a series of tutorials and demos highlighting the features and benefits of your software products. Include case studies and testimonials from satisfied customers to demonstrate the impact of your software on their financial success.

  4. Tax Tips and Strategies: Share videos offering valuable insights on tax planning, deductions, and filing, with a focus on strategies that can help viewers maximize their refunds and minimize their tax liabilities.

  5. Life Insurance and Financial Products: Develop content around various financial products, such as life insurance, annuities, and mutual funds. Explain the benefits and features of each product, and discuss how they can be integrated into a comprehensive wealth-building strategy.

  6. Global Financial Education: Explore financial topics from a global perspective, discussing investment opportunities, market trends, and financial practices in different countries. This content will help position Wealth Warriors as a global financial education provider.

  7. Success Stories: Share inspiring stories of individuals and businesses who have achieved financial success through Wealth Warriors' services and products. These testimonials can help build trust and credibility with your audience.

  8. Live Q&A Sessions: Host regular live-streamed sessions where viewers can ask questions and interact with your team of financial experts. This interactive format will help engage your audience and build a sense of community around your channel.

  9. Industry News and Updates: Keep your viewers informed about the latest developments in the financial world, including market trends, new financial products, and regulatory changes. Offer insights and analysis from your team of experts.

  10. Behind the Scenes: Give viewers a glimpse into the day-to-day operations of Wealth Warriors, showcasing the company culture, team members, and the passion that drives your mission.

By following this content plan, you can create a cohesive YouTube channel that promotes the entire range of services and products offered by Wealth Warriors, effectively reaching your target audience and building your brand's online presence.

Automating the content creation process can save time, reduce manual effort, and maintain consistency across your content. Here are some steps to automate content production:

  1. Content Calendar: Create a content calendar with a schedule for upcoming topics and publishing dates. This helps you stay organized and ensures you have a steady flow of content.

  2. Topic Research: Use tools like Google Trends, AnswerThePublic, and BuzzSumo to discover popular and relevant topics in your niche. Automate this process by setting up alerts and feeds to receive the latest information regularly.

  3. Keyword Research: Use tools like Google Keyword Planner, Ahrefs, or SEMrush to identify target keywords for your content. Set up regular reports to receive updated keyword suggestions.

  4. Content Templates: Develop templates for different content formats, such as blog posts, social media updates, and video scripts. This streamlines the content creation process and maintains consistency.

  5. Content Generation: Utilize AI-powered tools like OpenAI's GPT-3, Jarvis (Conversion.ai), or Copy.ai to generate content ideas, outlines, or even complete drafts. These tools can save time and provide inspiration for your content.

  6. Collaboration and Task Management: Use platforms like Trello, Asana, or Airtable to assign tasks, track progress, and manage deadlines. Set up automations to streamline communication and ensure timely completion of content.

  7. Content Review and Editing: Automate the editing process using tools like Grammarly or ProWritingAid, which can detect grammar and spelling errors, suggest improvements, and maintain consistent style and tone.

  8. Image and Video Creation: Use tools like Canva, Adobe Spark, or Lumen5 to create visuals and videos for your content. Automate image sourcing using platforms like Unsplash or Pexels that provide free stock images.

  9. Social Media Scheduling: Automate the publishing of your content on social media using tools like Buffer, Hootsuite, or Sprout Social. Schedule posts in advance, and set up automatic sharing across multiple platforms.

  10. Analytics and Reporting: Use tools like Google Analytics, SEMrush, or Ahrefs to track your content's performance. Set up automated reports and alerts to monitor metrics and make data-driven decisions for your content strategy.

Keep in mind that while automation can save time and reduce manual effort, it's essential to maintain a balance between automation and human touch. Engage with your audience, add your unique voice and perspective to the content, and ensure quality is not compromised due to excessive automation.

Integrating ChatGPT into your Wealth Warriors company can greatly enhance user experience and support your clients in achieving their financial goals. Here are some ways to implement ChatGPT and the benefits it can provide:

  1. Customer Support: Integrate ChatGPT into your website or app to serve as an AI-powered customer support chatbot. It can answer frequently asked questions, provide guidance on using your software, and troubleshoot issues. This can lead to faster resolution times and a more efficient support experience for your users.

  2. Personalized Financial Advice: ChatGPT can offer personalized financial tips and recommendations based on users' financial situations, goals, and preferences. While it is important to note that AI-generated advice should not replace professional financial advice, it can provide users with general guidance and suggestions.

  3. Content Generation: ChatGPT can help you generate content for your blog, social media, and YouTube channel. By automating part of the content creation process, you can save time and maintain a consistent output of informative and engaging material for your audience.

  4. Financial Calculators: Integrate ChatGPT into your software to create user-friendly financial calculators that offer insights into budgeting, debt repayment, savings goals, and investment projections. This can help users make informed decisions about their financial planning.

  5. Interactive Learning: Use ChatGPT to create interactive financial education materials, like quizzes, flashcards, and case studies. This can help users better understand complex financial concepts and make learning more engaging.

  6. Onboarding: Incorporate ChatGPT into your onboarding process to guide new users through setting up their accounts, inputting financial information, and learning about the software's features. This can enhance user experience and increase the likelihood of successful software adoption.

  7. Software Feature Recommendations: ChatGPT can analyze users' financial profiles and suggest software features or tools that might be helpful for their specific needs. This can encourage users to explore and make the most of your software's capabilities.

  8. Community Engagement: Utilize ChatGPT to manage a user forum or social media group where users can ask questions, share experiences, and learn from each other. By fostering a sense of community, you can increase user satisfaction and loyalty.

Remember, while integrating ChatGPT can provide numerous benefits, it is essential to ensure the AI-generated output is accurate and reliable. Regular monitoring and fine-tuning of the AI's responses, along with clear disclaimers about the limitations of AI-generated advice, will help maintain user trust and satisfaction.

o integrate an AI like ChatGPT, which you'd like to call "Legacy," into your Wealth Warriors company, follow these steps:

  1. Develop a clear AI strategy: Determine how Legacy will enhance your company's services and user experience. Identify the specific areas where the AI will be integrated, such as customer support, financial advice, content generation, or software feature recommendations.

  2. Select an AI framework: If you want to create your own AI model similar to ChatGPT, you'll need to choose a suitable AI framework like TensorFlow, PyTorch, or Hugging Face Transformers. Alternatively, you can use a pre-trained model like OpenAI's GPT-3 and fine-tune it to your specific use case.

  3. Collect and prepare data: Gather relevant data to train or fine-tune your AI model. This may include financial texts, user queries, and responses from experts. Clean and preprocess the data to ensure the AI's training is effective.

  4. Train or fine-tune the AI model: Using the prepared data, train your AI model or fine-tune an existing model like GPT-3 to align with your company's needs and goals. This step will require computational resources and expertise in machine learning.

  5. Test and validate the model: Evaluate the performance of your AI model by testing it on a variety of tasks related to your company's services. Continuously refine and improve the model based on feedback and performance metrics.

  6. Develop a user-friendly interface: Design an intuitive interface for your website or app that allows users to interact with Legacy easily. This could include a chat interface, voice assistant, or other interactive elements.

  7. Integrate the AI model: Connect your trained AI model to the user interface you've designed, integrating it with your existing software, website, or app.

  8. Monitor and maintain: Regularly monitor Legacy's performance and user interactions to ensure accuracy and reliability. Address any issues that arise and fine-tune the model as needed to maintain a high level of user satisfaction.

  9. Launch and promote: Announce the launch of Legacy to your users and potential clients, highlighting its features and benefits. Use marketing channels like your website, social media, email campaigns, and blog to promote the AI integration.

  10. Gather user feedback: Encourage users to provide feedback on their experiences with Legacy. Use this feedback to make improvements, enhance the AI's performance, and ensure it continues to meet user needs and expectations.

Remember that integrating an AI like ChatGPT requires expertise in machine learning and natural language processing. You may need to collaborate with AI experts, data scientists, or software engineers to successfully develop and implement Legacy in your Wealth Warriors company.

Legacy is a strong and memorable name for an AI-driven assistant in the context of your Wealth Warriors company. The name conveys a sense of continuity, heritage, and long-lasting impact, which can resonate with users who are focused on building and preserving their wealth for future generations. It also implies that your AI-driven assistant is designed to help users create a lasting financial legacy.

However, the most important factor when choosing a name is how well it aligns with your company's branding, vision, and the features your AI-driven assistant offers. If you feel that "Legacy" encapsulates the essence of your AI assistant and aligns with your company's goals, then it is a good choice.

Legacy, designed exclusively for Wealth Warriors users, is an advanced AI-driven assistant that aims to revolutionize your financial journey by providing personalized guidance, support, and resources to help you achieve your financial goals. By integrating seamlessly with our existing suite of services and products, Legacy empowers you with real-time insights and tailored recommendations to make the most of your wealth-building experience.

Some key features of Legacy include:

  1. Customer Support: Legacy offers prompt and efficient customer support, answering your queries about our services, software, and financial products. Accessible through our website or app, Legacy is available 24/7 to address your concerns and ensure a seamless user experience.

  2. Personalized Financial Guidance: Legacy provides general financial advice and recommendations based on your individual financial situation, goals, and preferences. While it does not replace professional financial advice, it serves as a valuable resource for users seeking quick and accessible guidance.

  3. Content Generation: Legacy helps curate a range of informative and engaging content, tailored to your interests and financial objectives. This includes articles, videos, and other resources that can help you stay informed and motivated on your wealth-building journey.

  4. Interactive Learning: Legacy supports your financial education by offering interactive learning experiences, such as quizzes, flashcards, and case studies. This makes learning complex financial concepts both fun and engaging.

  5. Software Feature Recommendations: Legacy analyzes your financial profile and suggests software features or tools that may be beneficial for your specific needs. This helps you explore and fully utilize our software's capabilities for optimal results.

  6. Community Engagement: Legacy fosters a sense of community by managing user forums or social media groups, where you can ask questions, share experiences, and learn from fellow Wealth Warriors members.

Please note that while Legacy is designed to offer accurate and reliable assistance, it is essential to use discretion when following AI-generated advice. Always consult a professional financial advisor for personalized and comprehensive guidance tailored to your specific situation.


Your Wealth Warriors formula seems to cover a comprehensive range of topics that are crucial to financial success. Here are a few thoughts on how it could be further optimized:

  1. Order: The order you've laid out is fairly logical. However, you could consider rearranging it as: Credit, Income, Performance, and Investments. Here's why:

  2. Start with Credit, as building good credit is foundational to financial health.

  3. Next, focus on Income, which is the next logical step after establishing good credit.

  4. Then, Performance. Once income is steady, one can focus on enhancing personal and business performance to increase that income and effectiveness.

  5. Finally, Investments. With strong credit, a stable income, and optimum performance, one is better positioned to invest wisely.

  6. Integration: It's not only about each component but also about how they integrate. Encourage the understanding that these components are not siloed but rather interconnected. Good credit affects the types of investments available to you, performance can impact income, etc. So, consider emphasizing the synergy between these components in your model.

  7. Education: Under each component, it would be beneficial to provide ongoing education. This could be through workshops, webinars, or online resources. It's not enough to simply help people in these areas; it's also important to equip them with the knowledge to manage these aspects independently in the future.

  8. Goal-Setting and Tracking: Help your clients set specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) goals for each component, and provide tools for tracking progress over time. This way, your clients can see how far they've come, which can be very motivating.

  9. Personalization: Different people have different needs, ambitions, and risk tolerance. Your model should take this into account and be adaptable enough to offer personalized advice.

In summary, your approach is comprehensive and covers the key aspects of financial success. The modifications suggested above aim to enhance the existing model, ensuring a more fluid transition between components, and facilitating a more personalized, educative, and goal-oriented experience for your clients.

Your formula covers the key components of financial success quite well, but there are a few more considerations that could add value to your approach:

  1. Budgeting and Saving: While this might seem like a subset of Income, it's so fundamental that it might deserve its own category. Teaching your clients how to manage their money, save effectively, and budget wisely is crucial.

  2. Risk Management and Insurance: Protecting one's wealth from unexpected life events is an important aspect of financial planning. This could include information on various types of insurance (like life, health, disability, and property insurance), and how to build an emergency fund.

  3. Tax Planning: Understanding taxes is essential for managing income and investments effectively. This component would cover areas like optimizing tax deductions, understanding tax implications of different investment strategies, and planning for future tax liabilities.

  4. Retirement Planning: This is a long-term goal for many people, and having a dedicated component that addresses it can be beneficial. This could include discussions on 401(k), IRA, Roth IRA, pension plans, and other retirement savings strategies.

  5. Estate Planning: This component involves planning for wealth transfer, including creating a will, setting up trusts, and understanding estate taxes.

  6. Philanthropy: Some people may wish to use part of their wealth to support charitable causes. Including this component could help them understand how they can give back in the most effective and tax-efficient way.

  7. Psychology of Money: Financial decisions are often influenced by one's emotions and mindset. Understanding this can help individuals avoid common pitfalls like impulsive spending or investment decisions driven by fear or greed.

Adding these components would certainly make your model more comprehensive, but it's also important to consider your audience. Not all components will be relevant to all clients, so a degree of flexibility and personalization would be beneficial.

Each of these categories represents a facet of financial wellness. Please note, these categories could be rearranged and renamed to suit the needs and understanding of your specific audience.

  2. Wealth Warrior Champion: The term "Champion" fits well with the "Warrior" theme and indicates a person who has mastered all four components.

  7. Wealth Warrior Luminary: "Luminary" refers to a person who inspires or influences others, and can signify someone who has reached an aspirational level of success.

  8. Wealth Warrior Paragon: "Paragon" represents a model of excellence or perfection.

  9. Wealth Warrior Virtuoso: "Virtuoso" signifies someone highly skilled in a particular field, in this case, financial management.

Remember to select a term that is not only aligned with your brand but also resonates with your target audience and their aspirations.

COO oversees daily operations

Job posting

Why join

As a small team, we work in a highly collaborative environment and you'll have the opportunity to participate in every part of the business from idea to production.

Impact: Build the foundation and shape engineering practices, team, and company culture.

Excellence: Practice your craft with other ICs in a well-organized, fast-paced environment.

Ownership: Influence the direction of product and strategy — we care about your opinions.

What you'll do (responsibilities)

We're looking for an experienced individual contributor who enjoys working alongside other experienced engineers and designers to quickly build and iterate on backend/API/platform.

  • Build the time layer for the Internet. You'll build the infrastructure for Cron from the ground up, having a huge and direct impact by shipping your work to users on prod daily.

  • Use modern web tech and influence the stack. The frontend is React, the (still minimal) backend Node/Express, and we use TypeScript across the full stack. As we build out our stack, you get to make critical choices and lay the foundations.

  • Self-direct your work and co-own the product. You're a technical founder type and will have autonomy and responsibility. You'll be involved in shaping the roadmap and will own Cron's exploding backend needs.

  • Create a robust and scalable backend. Build PostgreSQL database models, performant REST API with Rediscache, delta sync, and offline support using IndexedDB, 3rd party integrations, product analytics, transactional email, and service monitoring. We currently deploy to Heroku to keep DevOps simple and will be looking for you to establish viable long-term cloud infrastructure and operations.

  • Build UI components. You'll implement basic UI based on Figma mocks and our design system. You'll collaborate with designers and frontend engineers on user-facing features powered by your backend code. We rapidly ship UI that has a native feel to it by polishing CSS, interaction states, and animations.

  • Solve interesting technical problems. Bring your full creativity to solve super-challenging technical problems: from complex backend architecture with 3rd party integrations, syncing app state, to real-time collaboration.

What we're looking for (qualifications)

You're a senior IC that has built such systems before and this is not an area you have to ramp up on. We don't require any formal qualifications but value learning new skills — especially from one another. We are looking for someone that feels a sense of duty to the users of their work.

  • Highly productive while producing quality code. You enjoy pushing out features in a pragmatic and maintainable way. You know when to use duct tape and when to lay a foundation.

  • Curious and quick learning. We don't expect you to have experience in every technology we use, but to learn and be productive quickly. Owning several repos and jumping into all of them doesn't scare you.

  • Design sensibility. While you'll co-craft the interface with top designers and frontend engineers, we expect you to have a knack for great UX, such that you feel if something is off and can flag it, or better yet, polish it.

  • Attention to detail while pragmatic. We strive for few slips in code, Git hygiene, and clear written communication — all while remaining low-ego and simply focusing on solutions.

  • Interested in productivity apps/systems. You might use your calendar to time block, try out Chrome extensions, configure custom app launchers, or self-optimize in other ways.

  • Good heart. We don't tolerate jerks and are generally just friendly people.

What we offer (compensation & benefits)

We'll treat you well. If there are any other benefits that are important to you, we'd like to hear.

  • Competitive salary and equity — multiple options based on your desire for ownership.

  • Paid time off — 4 weeks paid vacation, paid sick leave, and paid parental leave.

  • Fully-distributed culture — live and work where you'd like (US–EU time zones).

  • Co-working space — company-paid co-working desk in your local community.

  • Hardware setup — new MacBook Pro, big display, and accessories.

How to Apply

Interested in learning more about what it's like to build Cron with us? We'd love to talk! Email our founder Raphael Schaad directly at raphael@cron.com.

  • Include this role's title in your subject line.

  • Send along links that best showcase the relevant things you've built and done.

  • Tell us briefly why you're interested in joining Cron.

Diversity and inclusion are core to our culture. If you are a member of an underrepresented group in tech, we strongly encourage you to apply.

Is this role not the right fit? If you resonate with our mission and think your profile would be a great fit, send an email to jobs@cron.com and pass along any information you believe is relevant.

VI. “Things To Do Before, During and After a Podcast” Checklist

To be an awesome podcast guest, make sure you follow the checklist below. It will help you prepare yourself, relax and build a great relationship with the audience and the host.

Send your book in advanced to the podcast host

BEFORE THE PODCAST

  • Listen to two full episodes

  • Write down the typical audience member, and why they listen

  • Read show reviews on Chartable or Listen Notes

  • Note any common questions or “bits” the show uses

  • Prepare at least 3 stories that you can unfurl

  • Do any requested pre-work early and completely

DURING THE PODCAST

  • Have the best possible audio set up

  • Use the host(s) name

  • Keep answers concise

  • Don’t ask for a do-over unless it’s BAD

  • Reference prior episodes, if relevant

  • Have a CTA/offer, etc. for listeners

AFTER THE PODCAST

  • Send a thank you note to host (video is best)

  • Promote the episode as much as possible, and tag host(s) in social

  • Offer to connect host(s) to relevant future guests

  • Gently ask host(s) for recommendations to related shows (wait 2 weeks for this)

Youtube Video Upload Checklist

  • Plan Your Videos in AdvanceResearch and plan your videos, considering your audience and topics of interest. Plan your next 10 videos based on these insights.

  • Produce High-Quality VideosEnsure HD quality, stabilize your videos, use good audio equipment, and have decent lighting.

  • Edit Your VideosUse editing to tell your story and create a unique style. Editing can make your content stand out.

  • Decide How You Will UploadChoose between public, private, or unlisted settings for your videos. Utilize the scheduling feature to maintain a consistent posting schedule.

  • Descriptions, Titles & Tags Don't neglect your metadata. Proper descriptions, titles, and tags are crucial for your videos to be found and viewed on YouTube.

  • Upload Custom Thumbnails Quality thumbnails are essential for attracting viewers. Use custom thumbnails to make your videos more appealing.

  • Share Videos in Social Media Distribute your videos on social media platforms where your audience is present. Engagement in the first 48 hours can impact video rankings and exposure.

  • Use YouTube Info Cards Info Cards can enhance engagement and can be used to link to other videos, playlists, fan funding, other channels, and polls.

  • Add Your Video to a PlaylistPlaylists can increase discovery on YouTube, boost watch time, and keep your channel organized.

  • **Use Closed Captions (Maybe)**Closed captions can be beneficial for an international audience and differently-abled viewers, and may help with discovery in YouTube search.

  • Monetize Your VideosMonetizing your videos can provide opportunities to earn revenue and reinvest in your channel.

  • Enable/Disable Comments Decide whether to enable or disable comments based on the nature of your video and desired audience engagement.

  • Check Your Videos in Search Use tools like Tube Buddy to see how your videos perform in YouTube searches and adjust your keywords, tags, titles, and descriptions accordingly.

  • Analyze Your Video Data Use the YouTube Dashboard to measure the success of your videos, including watch time, retention rates, and subscriber growth.

  • Watch and Review Your Videos Continuously evaluate your videos for improvements to ensure each new video is better than the last.

2. Identify market gaps and opportunities.

3. Analyze competitor marketing strategies and positioning.

4. Compile a competitor feature and pricing comparison.

Strategy Development

1. Segment the market based on demographic, psychographic, and behavioral data.

2. Create detailed buyer personas.

3. Set specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) marketing goals.

4. Align marketing objectives with overall business targets.

Multi-Channel Marketing Plan

1. Develop a content calendar outlining topics, formats, and publishing schedules.

2. Determine content creation resources and responsibilities.

3. Evaluate the effectiveness of various channels (social media, email, SEO, etc.).

4. Choose channels based on target audience preferences and marketing goals.

Implementation and Execution

1. Execute marketing campaigns across selected channels.

2. Monitor campaign performance and adjust strategies as needed.

3. Ensure sales team is informed about marketing campaigns and provided with necessary materials.

4. Set up a system for lead sharing and feedback between sales and marketing.

Measurement and Optimization

1. Identify key performance indicators (KPIs) for each marketing channel and campaign.

2. Implement tools for tracking and analysis.

3. Regularly review campaign data to assess performance against KPIs.

4. Conduct A/B testing to optimize marketing messages and channels.

5. Gather insights from campaign performance and market feedback.

Unified Portal with Zoho Creator

To create a unified portal that combines information from multiple organizations, you can use Zoho Creator. Here’s how you can set it up:

  1. Create Custom Portals in Zoho Creator:

  2. Use Zoho Creator to develop custom portals where data from different Zoho apps and organizations can be displayed.

  3. Use Zoho Creator’s drag-and-drop interface to design the portal without needing extensive coding knowledge.

  4. Data Integration with Zoho Flow:

  5. Use Zoho Flow to automate data synchronization between different Zoho organizations.

  6. Create workflows in Zoho Flow to pull data from Zoho Books, Zoho Subscriptions, and Zoho Checkout into the unified portal.

  7. SSO and Custom Links:

  8. Implement SSO with Auth0 to allow users to log in once and access all integrated services.

  9. Use custom links within the portal to direct users to specific areas in Circle.so based on their purchases and subscriptions.

  10. Centralized CRM and Support:

  11. Use Zoho CRM as the central hub for managing customer data.

  12. Integrate Zoho Desk for managing support tickets across all organizations.

  13. Tracking and Management:

  14. Ensure that all financial transactions and subscriptions are routed correctly to the respective organizations while being visible in a centralized CRM system.

  15. Use Zoho Analytics for detailed reporting and tracking across multiple organizations.

Summary

By leveraging multiple Zoho instances for different organizations and using Zoho Creator and Zoho Flow for integration, you can create a unified platform. This setup allows you to manage subscriptions, invoices, and customer support from a centralized portal while maintaining separate financial records for each organization. This approach ensures a seamless customer experience and efficient management of all your business processes.

Synchronization and Workflow

Central Calendar Integration:

  • Use Zoho Calendar as the central hub for all scheduling.

  • Sync Apple Calendar with Zoho Calendar to have a unified view of personal and business events.

  • Subscribe to TickTick calendar feed in Zoho Calendar for personal tasks.

Task and Project Management:

  • Use TickTick for personal tasks and projects. Sync important tasks to Zoho Calendar.

  • Manage business projects in Zoho Projects and business tasks in Zoho Tasks.

  • Utilize Zoho Flow and Zoho Orchestly for automations between these tools.

File Management:

  • Store personal files in iCloud and business files in Zoho WorkDrive.

  • Use 1Password for secure storage of sensitive personal and business information.

Note and Information Capture:

  • Capture notes and ideas in Zoho Notebook for both personal and business use.

  • Use Notion for creating and sharing templates, managing personal projects, and storing examples for students.

Bookmarks and Link Management:

  • Use Raindrop.io for personal bookmark management (optional) or Zoho Notebook for an integrated solution.

  • Linktree for managing business and social media links.

Recommendations for Elimination and Streamlining

  1. Remove Monday.com, Sync.com, and Raindrop.io (if you choose to integrate bookmarks into Zoho Notebook).

  2. Centralize all task management using TickTick for personal tasks and Zoho Tasks for business tasks.

  3. Consolidate file storage into iCloud for personal use and Zoho WorkDrive for business use.

  4. Unify calendars by syncing Apple Calendar with Zoho Calendar.

  5. Streamline note-taking and document management with Zoho Notebook and Notion.

Requirements for the Unified Portal

1. Unified Customer Portal

  • Platform: WordPress with ZPortals

    • Functionality:Integrate Zoho CRM, Zoho Books, Zoho Subscriptions, Zoho Desk.

    • Allow customers to view and manage their subscriptions, invoices, and support tickets.

2. Integration of Multiple Zoho Organizations

    • Challenges:Zoho One is designed for a single organization. Integrating multiple organizations requires a customized approach.

3. Centralized Data Management

    • Tools Required:Zoho CRM: For managing customer data across all organizations.

    • Zoho Books: For managing invoicing and accounting from different organizations.

    • Zoho Subscriptions: For managing recurring billing across different services.

    • Zoho Desk: For managing support tickets.

4. Data Synchronization

    • Process:Use Zoho Flow to automate data synchronization between different Zoho applications and organizations.

    • Create workflows to sync customer data, payment information, and support tickets across different Zoho organizations into a centralized Zoho CRM instance.

5. Custom Portal Development

    • Tools Required:Zoho Creator: To develop custom portals that can pull data from multiple Zoho organizations.

    • WordPress with ZPortals: For a user-friendly front-end interface.

Summary

To integrate and manage multiple Zoho organizations, you'll need separate Zoho instances for each type of service provided by each company. This setup requires a unified portal to centralize all customer interactions and data management. By leveraging Zoho CRM, Zoho Books, Zoho Subscriptions, Zoho Desk, and Zoho Flow, you can create a seamless and integrated system that handles all your business needs efficiently.


Zoho App Portals

Zoho Applications with Portal Capabilities:

1. Zoho CRM:

Customer Portal:

  • Purpose: Allow customers to manage their support tickets, access the knowledge base, update their contact information, and view invoices.

    1. Features:Support Ticket Management: Customers can raise, view, and manage their support tickets.

    2. Knowledge Base Access: Customers can search and access articles in the knowledge base.

    3. Profile Updates: Customers can update their contact information.

    4. Invoice Viewing: Customers can view their past invoices and transaction history.

2. Zoho Desk:

Customer Support Portal:

  • Purpose: Enable customers to raise, view, and manage their support tickets and access self-help articles.

    1. Features:Ticket Submission: Customers can submit new support tickets.

    2. Ticket Tracking: Customers can track the status and updates of their tickets.

    3. Knowledge Base: Customers can access self-help articles to resolve issues on their own.

    4. Community Forums: Customers can participate in community discussions and seek help from other users.

3. Zoho Projects:

Client Portal:

  • Purpose: Facilitate project collaboration, task management, and file sharing with clients.

    1. Features:Project Tracking: Clients can view project progress and timelines.

    2. Task Management: Clients can see assigned tasks and their statuses.

    3. File Sharing: Securely share project-related files with clients.

    4. Discussions: Clients can participate in project discussions and provide feedback.

4. Zoho Creator:

Custom Portals:

  • Purpose: Build tailored portals for various business applications, such as vendor management, employee self-service, or customer feedback systems.

    1. Features:Custom Workflows: Create custom workflows to automate business processes.

    2. Role-Based Access: Define access permissions based on user roles.

    3. Form Customization: Customize forms for data collection and management.

    4. Report Generation: Generate custom reports based on collected data.

5. Zoho Books:

Client Portal:

  • Purpose: Streamline financial interactions between businesses and their clients by allowing them to view and pay invoices, manage estimates, and access transaction history.

    1. Features:Invoice Management: Clients can view, download, and pay their invoices.

    2. Estimate Approval: Clients can view and approve estimates, which can be converted into invoices.

    3. Transaction History: Clients have access to their complete transaction history.

    4. Payment Gateway Integration: Clients can make secure online payments.

6. Zoho Subscriptions:

Client Portal:

  • Purpose: Allow customers to manage their subscriptions, view billing history, and update payment information.

    1. Features:Subscription Management: Customers can upgrade, downgrade, or cancel their subscriptions.

    2. Payment Methods: Customers can securely add, update, or remove their payment methods.

    3. Invoice Access: Customers can view and download past invoices.

    4. Transaction History: Customers can review their complete transaction history.

7. Zoho WorkDrive:

Document Sharing Portal:

  • Purpose: Securely share and collaborate on documents with clients or team members.

    1. Features:File Sharing: Share documents with defined access permissions.

    2. Collaboration: Collaborate on documents in real-time.

    3. Activity Tracking: Track document activity and changes.

    4. Version Control: Maintain version control of documents.

8. Zoho Forms:

Data Collection Portal:

  • Purpose: Create and share forms through a portal for collecting customer feedback, survey responses, registrations, or other data.

    1. Features:Form Creation: Design custom forms for various purposes.

    2. Data Management: Collect and manage data submissions.

    3. Integration: Integrate forms with other Zoho apps for seamless data flow.

    4. Reporting: Generate reports based on collected data.

9. Zoho Sites:

Membership Portals:

  • Purpose: Create websites with restricted content access for members, such as exclusive articles, videos, or resources.

    1. Features:Content Restriction: Restrict access to specific content for members only.

    2. Custom Pages: Create custom pages and sections for members.

    3. User Management: Manage member registrations and profiles.

    4. Payment Integration: Integrate with payment gateways for membership fees.

10. Zoho Vault:

Password Management Portal:

  • Purpose: Provide secure password management for teams and individuals, ensuring safe access to shared credentials.

    1. Features:Password Storage: Securely store and manage passwords.

    2. Access Control: Define access permissions for shared credentials.

    3. Audit Trails: Track and monitor password usage.

    4. Single Sign-On (SSO): Enable SSO for seamless access across Zoho applications.

11. Zoho Commerce:

E-commerce Portal:

  • Purpose: Create an online store to sell products and services, with customer access to order history and tracking.

    1. Features:Product Management: Manage product listings and inventory.

    2. Order Tracking: Allow customers to track their orders.

    3. Payment Processing: Integrate with payment gateways for secure transactions.

    4. Customer Accounts: Provide customers with accounts to view their order history and manage their profiles.

12. Zoho Survey:

Survey Portal:

  • Purpose: Collect customer feedback, conduct surveys, and analyze responses through a user-friendly portal.

    1. Features:Survey Creation: Design and distribute surveys.

    2. Response Collection: Collect and manage survey responses.

    3. Reporting: Analyze survey results and generate reports.

    4. Customization: Customize surveys with branding and specific questions.

Setting Up Client Portals:

General Steps for Enabling Portals:

    • Enable Portal:Navigate to the relevant settings within each Zoho application (e.g., Settings > Client Portal in Zoho Books).

    • Enable the portal functionality and configure the options to match your business requirements.

    • Invite Clients:Send invitations to clients from within the application, enabling them to access their respective portals.

    • Customize Portal Appearance:Adjust the look and feel of the portal to align with your branding and provide a consistent user experience.

Benefits of Using Zoho Portals:

  1. Improved Communication: Centralized platforms for communication reduce the need for back-and-forth emails.

  2. Enhanced Customer Experience: Clients have access to relevant information in one place, improving transparency and satisfaction.

  3. Self-Service Convenience: Clients can manage their own data, reducing administrative workload for your team.

  4. Automated Processes: Save time and minimize errors with automated notifications and workflows.

  5. Security: Secure access with role-based permissions and robust data protection measures.

  6. Integration: Seamless integration with other Zoho applications ensures a unified experience across your business operations.

By leveraging these portal functionalities across various Zoho applications, businesses can enhance operational efficiency, improve customer engagement, and provide a better overall experience for their clients and team members.

Zoho Sites Management & Scaling Guide

Website Management and Scaling Guide for Zoho Sites

Key Principles for Managing and Scaling Your Website

1. Optimize Website Performance

  • Clean Up Database: Regularly clean your website database to improve performance and reduce load times. Tools like Advanced Database Cleaner can help streamline this process.

  • Image Optimization: Compress images to reduce file sizes without compromising quality using tools like EWWW Image Optimizer.

  • Leverage Caching: Use caching mechanisms like Redis Cache to speed up website loading times and enhance user experience.

2. Monitor Website Health

  • Server Performance Tracking: Monitor your server health using tools like WP Server Stats to ensure your website remains stable and fast.

  • Performance Testing: Run periodic tests using tools like WPPerformanceTester or WPBenchmark to assess and improve site performance.

3. Enhance User Experience

  • Minimize Autoloaded Data: Limit unnecessary autoloaded data to keep your site lightweight and responsive.

  • Utilize Content Delivery Networks (CDNs): Distribute content across global servers to reduce latency for users worldwide.

4. Scaling Strategies for High-Traffic Websites

  • Database Optimization: Consider database solutions like MariaDB or MySQL to handle growing data needs effectively.

  • Server Scaling: Upgrade your hosting plan or move to cloud-based solutions for higher traffic capacity.

  • Advanced Caching: Implement tools like LiteSpeed Cache to manage increased traffic while maintaining fast load times.

5. Integrate Third-Party Tools with Zoho Sites

  • Automation Tools: Use platforms like Zapier to connect Zoho Sites with other business applications for streamlined workflows.

  • Analytics and Reporting: Track visitor behavior and performance metrics using Zoho’s built-in tools or integrate with external platforms.

6. Regular Maintenance Practices

  • Update PHP Versions: Keep your site’s PHP version updated for better performance and security.

  • Remove Unused Plugins: Deactivate and delete unnecessary plugins to avoid bloat.

  • Backup Regularly: Use automated backup solutions to secure your website data.

Tools Mentioned

  • Perfmatters: Optimize your website’s speed by disabling unnecessary features.

  • Redis Cache: Improve load times by caching frequently used data.

  • EWWW Image Optimizer: Reduce image file sizes for faster loading.

  • Advanced Database Cleaner: Maintain a clean and efficient database.

Conclusion

By implementing these strategies, you can ensure your Zoho Sites website remains fast, scalable, and user-friendly. Regular maintenance and optimization will help you provide an excellent user experience while supporting your growth objectives.

Note: Adapt these strategies as needed to suit your specific website and business requirements.

Performance Management


Potential Job Positions

  1. Account Executive: Focuses on building client relationships by offering solutions and support, managing contracts, and driving sales.

  2. Accounting: Manages financial records and ensures the accuracy of financial reporting.

  3. Analyst: Responsible for gathering and interpreting data to support business decisions.

  4. Architect: Designs buildings or systems and ensures their functionality and safety.

  5. Assistant: Provides administrative support and helps with daily tasks to ensure efficient operations.

  6. Automation Architect: Designs and implements automation solutions to improve processes and workflows.

  7. CDO (Chief Data Officer): Oversees data management strategy, governance, and policy development.

  8. CEO (Chief Executive Officer): The highest-ranking executive in a company, responsible for overall operations, making major corporate decisions, managing the overall resources and operations of a company.

  9. CFO (Chief Financial Officer): Manages the financial actions of a company, including tracking cash flow and financial planning.

  10. Chairman: Leads and sets the agenda for the board of directors, providing oversight and guidance to the CEO and other executives.

  11. Chief Architect: Oversees the creation of technology architectures and ensures alignment with the business objectives.

  12. Chief Scientist: Leads scientific research and development within a company.

  13. CIO (Chief Information Officer): Oversees the information technology (IT) needs of an organization.

  14. CISO (Chief Information Security Officer): Responsible for an organization's information and data security.

  15. CMO (Chief Marketing Officer): Leads the marketing efforts and strategy of a company.

  16. Compliance Officer: Ensures a company complies with external laws and regulations as well as internal policies and bylaws.

  17. Consultant: Provides expert advice in a particular area such as security (cybersecurity consultant), management, education, accountancy, law, human resources, marketing (and public relations), finance, engineering, science, or any of many other specialized fields.

  18. COO (Chief Operating Officer): Oversees the organization's ongoing operations and procedures.

  19. CTO (Chief Technology Officer): Focuses on scientific and technological issues within an organization.

  20. Data Scientist: Uses statistical methods to analyze and interpret data to help drive decision-making.

  21. Database Administrator: Uses software to store and organize data, such as financial information and customer shipping records.

  22. Developer: Creates and maintains software applications.

  23. Director: Manages one or multiple departments within a company and strategizes for operational or programmatic activities.

  24. Engineer: Applies scientific knowledge to design, build, and analyze machines, structures, and other items.

  25. Executive: Performs high-level tasks and decision-making processes within a company.

  26. Finance: Manages the company's financial actions, including budgeting, forecasting, and investments.

  27. General Counsel: The chief lawyer of a legal department within a company or government department.

  28. IT Auditor: Evaluates and improves the effectiveness of risk management, control, and governance processes in an organization.

  29. Lawyer: Practices law by advising and representing clients in legal matters.

  30. Legal Services: Provides various legal support and services for the organization.

  31. Manager: Oversees the operations of a department or group within a company.

  32. Media: Works with various communication channels and tools to create, convey, or exchange information.

  33. Network Administrator: Maintains computing environments, including computer networks, systems, applications, and communications.

  34. Owner: The proprietor of a business.

  35. Partner: Shares ownership of a legal entity or business along with other partners.

  36. President: Often a senior executive in charge of a significant business unit or the entire company.

  37. Press: Involved in newsgathering and reporting for media outlets.

  38. Procurement: Responsible for acquiring goods or services for the organization.

  39. Product Manager: Oversees the development and lifecycle of a product.

  40. Programmer: Writes computer code to create software programs.

  41. Purchasing: Responsible for buying goods, services, or works from an external source.

  42. Solicitor: A legal practitioner who traditionally deals with most of the legal matters in some jurisdictions.

  43. Student: A person formally engaged in learning, especially at a school or other educational institution.

  44. System Admin (Systems Administrator): Ensures the efficient operation of a company’s network systems.

  45. Vice President: An executive that may rank just below the president or CEO and can have varying responsibilities and duties.

  46. Webmaster: Maintains and updates websites.

This list includes general descriptions, and the specific duties of these roles can vary widely depending on the industry and individual company.

Certainly! Continuing from number 47, here's a list of IT and corporate positions and departments along with a brief description of their functions:

  1. IT - Applications / Development: Focuses on the creation, maintenance, and implementation of software applications.

  2. IT - Business Intelligence: Uses data analytics to provide actionable insights for business decisions and strategy.

  3. IT - Database: Manages and maintains the company’s databases, ensuring data integrity, performance, and accessibility.

  4. IT - Desktop / Help Desk: Provides technical support to end-users, addressing issues related to desktop computers and peripherals.

  5. IT - Network: Responsible for the maintenance and administration of the company's computer networks.

  6. IT - Operations: Oversees the day-to-day operations of the IT department, ensuring systems run efficiently and effectively.

  7. IT - Project Management: Manages IT projects, ensuring they meet deadlines, stay within budget, and achieve the intended outcomes.

  8. IT - Quality / Testing: Ensures the quality of software and systems through rigorous testing and evaluation.

  9. IT - Risk / Compliance / Security: Manages risks related to IT, ensures compliance with regulations, and protects the company’s digital assets from security threats.

  10. IT - Server / Storage: Handles the servers and storage infrastructure, focusing on data management, backup, and recovery processes.

  11. IT - Telecom: Manages the company's telecommunication systems, including telephones, video conferencing, and internet access.

  12. IT - Web: Takes care of web-related services and infrastructure, including website development and maintenance.

Continuing into other corporate areas:

  1. Customer Service / Call Center: Handles customer inquiries and issues, providing support and information as needed.

  2. Executive Office: The central command of the company, including top executives and their direct support staff.

  3. Finance: Manages the company’s financial planning, tracking, and reporting.

  4. Human Resources: Handles recruitment, training, employee relations, benefits, and compliance with labor laws.

  5. Legal: Deals with all legal matters, including contracts, disputes, and regulatory compliance.

  6. Marketing Communications: Creates and distributes marketing materials and communications to promote the company’s brand and products.

  7. Research & Development: Develops new products or services and improves existing ones through research and innovation.

  8. Sales: Responsible for selling the company’s products or services and managing relationships with clients and customers.

These categories help structure a company's various roles and departments to clarify responsibilities and streamline operations.

Employee Benefits Example

Benefits

Health Insurance

For teammates in the US, the company covers 100% of health care, dental, and vision coverage. 🙌 You can view the insurance portal for plan specifics.

Paid Time Off

Everyone gets 4 weeks of paid time off in addition to official holidays. Please log your time off in the company calendar so others are aware.

We also take off Fridays during the summer months of June, July, and August. Enjoy the extra time and the warm weather! 🌞

Parental Leave

Everyone receives 1 month of parental leave when you bring a new little one into your family. You can use this all at one time or you can space it out over the first 6 months. Note: if your country has required rules around parental leave, you can follow them and just let your manager know.

Retirement Plan

For US folks, we have a company 401K that hooks right into our payroll portal. The company will match the first 6% of your contributions. We recommend everyone take advantage of the matching because… free money.

Education Allowance

We are all lifelong learners here. Here's how the company supports you in this:

  • unlimited ebooks for free

  • $2000 budget per year for attending conferences

  • any online class you think would be helpful

Matching Charitable Gifts

We believe that generosity is the best way to live. We'd love to encourage everyone to support people and causes they care about. Because of this, the company will match every dollar you give to a non-profit up to $20,000.

Coworking Space Stipend

If you prefer to use a co-working space, the company will pay for it. Just set up the billing through your Stripe card.

Travel & Expenses

  • Unless agreed upon otherwise, everyone should book their own flights and accomodations using your company credit card.

  • When booking travel, consider what you would pick if you were using your own money.

  • Any purchase over $50 needs a receipt.

Recruitment and Onboarding


Remote Onboarding Checklist

For anyone starting a new role, especially in a remote work environment, it can be daunting to catch up on tasks and become familiar with the work culture. However, a successful onboarding process can provide structure and security for new team members. Remote teams have the advantage of using tools like Slack, Zoom, and popular CRMs, which enable collaborations and communication that can sometimes be even clearer than in-person interactions.

Just like with any onboarding, your goals should be to empower your new hire and ensure a positive start to their employee journey.

WHAT TO EXPECT: We break down the onboarding process into four phases within the first 90 days of your new employee's journey. Feel free to restructure it as you see fit.

PHASE 1: PRE-ONBOARDING

right after acceptance letter, before start date

Send Over New Hire Paperwork:

  • Welcome note

  • Employee Agreement

  • Non-Disclosure Agreement, Non-compete or other legal documents

  • IRS forms (W-4 or W-9))

  • Direct deposit forms

  • Benefit documents

  • Employee Handbook or Welcome Packet

  • Information on work culture, employee resource groups (ERGs), core values

Send over tech for set-up:

  • Laptop

  • Monitor

  • Phone

  • Mouse

  • Keyboard

  • Headset

  • Team swag (coffee mug, apparel, stationary, etc. *onboarding kits from services like Swagup are great ways to surprise & delight

  • Contact information to IT if needed

Set up online accounts or send invites:

  • Company email address

  • Add to relevant email distribution lists

  • Any external communication invite (Slack, MS Teams, Zoom, etc.)

  • Company HRIS of engagement software

  • Password management software

  • Product management software (Trello, Asana, etc.)

Ad-hoc prep:

  • Reach out to team to schedule their own 1:1s to welcome new teammate

  • Assign welcome mentor from team

PHASE 2: WELCOMING & LEARNING THE ROPES

first day and first week or so.

Welcome meeting for first day:

  • Review org chart and day-to-day

  • Tour digital office set-up

  • Review role expectations

Manager checklist:

  • Schedule any needed 1:1s

  • Send invite to all relevant meetings

  • Give access to relevant Shared Drives, Project Management Boards, or Documents

  • Align with cross-functional stakeholders

  • Create onboarding project

  • Send new hire announcement to team

  • Send e-gift card for lunch or coffee for their first day*

typically you'd take them out for coffee or lunch if you were in office

Orientation

  • Give time to set-up online accounts

  • Tech set-up

  • Complete any new hire paperwork

  • Discuss benefits and insurance

  • Any necessary HR modules

  • Review company culture and core values

  • Review any technology or safety policies where needed

  • Employee support and resources

PHASE 3: TRAINING & ASSIMILATING TO ROLE

following first week

  • Review 3-month roadmap for key projects, trainings, and personal goals

  • Provide additional resources for any needed training

PHASE 3: TRAINING & ASSIMILATING TO ROLE

dependent on start date

  • Host 30-day check-in

  • Host 60-day check-in

  • Host 90-day check-in

  • Send onboarding survey or host feedback call on process

The onboarding process is an extension of your employee engagement strategy, and an intentional, well-planned and communicated approach will help your excited new hire feel at home in the company, even if they ’re working from home.

Bamboo HR PTO Policy Builder

How much time off is too much or too little? What types of PTO should you offer? In most companies, it's up to HR pros to answer these questions, build effective policies, and solve other time-off challenges.

We’ve compiled a list of questions and advice and a sample PTO policy to help you develop the perfect PTO policy for your company, including:

  • Building a solution that fits the needs of your employees and your business

  • Refining your larger compensation package.

  • Handling any PTO situations that arise.

Use this policy builder as a template to answer questions, compile research, and begin outlining your PTO policy. Click “Use Template,” in the upper right-hand corner, and a copy of this doc will be added to your Google Drive.

In 2022 alone, BambooHR helped companies manage more than 21 million time off requests. Our easy-to-use software combines time tracking, payroll, PTO, and more in one seamless platform designed to set you free to do great work. You can learn more about BambooHR here or schedule a demo here.

Important: Please keep in mind as you build or overhaul your PTO policy, you should consult with your legal counsel to ensure your policy complies with local labor laws and regulations.
