Sample PTO Policy


Lay Your Policy’s Foundation

An essential part of your PTO policy is communicating it to your employees. Be sure to document your employee time-off policy and provide all relevant details.

  • Add it to your employee handbook.

  • Make sure every manager and employee is familiar with it.

  • Review it with new hires during onboarding.

This will go a long way toward helping managers treat employees fairly while helping employees understand and follow the rules.


Types of PTO You May Offer

Vacation Time

While the average US worker gets 11 days of paid vacation each year, the number you offer is entirely up to you. We do encourage you to do industry-specific research to see what’s standard in your industry. You may also consider increasing paid vacation based on employee tenure.

Time off is an important benefit for employees, and matching or exceeding industry standards will help you remain competitive in the marketplace, mitigate burnout, and keep employees engaged.

Holidays

Private US companies aren't legally required to give employees paid time off for federal holidays. But depending on your industry, it’s best practice to at least give time off for major holidays. (We get that hospitals and places of the like need to keep doors open.)

Here’s a list of major US federal holidays you may consider giving your employees off:

  • New Year’s Day

  • Martin Luther King Jr. Day

  • President’s Day

  • Memorial Day

  • Juneteenth

  • Independence Day

  • Labor Day

  • Columbus/Indigenous People’s Day

  • Veteran’s Day

  • Thanksgiving Day

  • Christmas Day

You may also offer “floating holidays,” or a full day off that employees can use at their discretion. As not everyone celebrates the same holidays, it can be helpful to give your people options.

Whether you decide to give federal holidays off or supplement set holidays off with floating holidays, you should clearly communicate with employees, so they can plan accordingly.

Sick Leave

The pandemic made it clear that being able to take time off to recover from an illness is incredibly important. Employees can focus on recovering rather than trying to complete work in a fever haze (and spreading illness to other workers).

But mental health is just as important as physical health, so consider building “personal days” into your sick leave policy as well.

Bereavement Leave

In the case of the death of a loved one, bereavement leave allows employees to take time away from work to grieve, make funeral arrangements, and attend memorial services.

In your bereavement leave policy, you’ll need to decide:

  • Duration: How many PTO days are allowed per instance?

  • Eligibility: Which relationships qualify for bereavement leave?

  • Notification Process: As these instances tend to happen with little notice, will the request process differ from regular time-off requests?

  • Documentation: Will you require documented proof for bereavement leave?

Jury Duty and Civic Duty

Jury duty comes for us all eventually, and unfortunately, it may require an employee to miss a few days every once in a while. Consult your local laws and regulations to determine how you should handle paid time off for jury duty, and clearly outline your policy, so there are no questions when this inevitably comes up.

Parental Leave

A new baby or newly adopted child is a major change for your employees. It’s up to you how much time you’ll give off, but keep in mind that federal law guarantees 12 weeks of unpaid leave in the event of a birth or adoption.

Beyond the letter of the law, paid parental leave is incredibly important for helping your people and their family recover and bond with a new child. Some companies choose to create separate maternal leave and paternal leave policies, and some choose to create a blanket parental leave policy for all new parents.


PTO Policy Questions You Need to Answer

As you outline your policy, here are questions you’ll need to discuss with your HR and leadership team, so your managers and employees can appropriately plan their schedules. These are all questions your employees will frequently have, so be sure to make a written version of your policy or an FAQ easily accessible to all employees.

Write out an answer to each question, and you’ll be well on your way to having a built-out PTO policy. Some of these answers you’ll want to be sure to put in your PTO policy, and others will help you think about your policy’s fairness and whether it’s a good fit for your business.

  1. Who is eligible for PTO?

    • Is there a waiting period after being hired?

    • Do part-time employees get the same amount of time as full-time employees?

    • Are policies different for exempt and non-exempt employees?

  2. How do employees make PTO requests?

    • Do they need to make requests a certain amount of time in advance?

    • What happens if an employee has to make a last-minute PTO request?

    • Who will approve or deny PTO requests?

  3. How is PTO granted?

    • Are employees given all of their days for the year upfront?

    • Does PTO accrue over time? What’s the accrual rate?

    • Do employees get more PTO the longer they’re employed?

  4. How do employees check their PTO balance?

    • Is it available in your HR software?

    • Will they need to contact the HR department?

  5. How do you keep track of how much time off people have taken?

  6. Does unused PTO carry over to the next year?

    • Is there a maximum number of days employees can carry over?

    • Are there different policies for different types of PTO? (E.g., vacation time carries over, but sick leave doesn't.)

  7. Is unused PTO paid out upon termination of employment?

  8. Are there days or time periods when employees can’t request time off?

    • Is there a specific policy around requesting time off close to holidays?

  9. What happens if there are overlapping time-off requests on a team?

Example solutions:

  • First Come, First Served: The first to request gets the time off.

  • Reason-Based: Weigh and prioritize the reasons for the time-off requests.

  • Prior Request History: Those who have taken less time off get first dibs.

  • Seniority-Based: Whoever has been at the company longer gets priority.

  • Is there a minimum amount of time off employees are required to take?

  • What happens if an employee is out of PTO but needs to take more time off?

    • Is unpaid time off allowed?

  • Do we want to give employees any “special” days off? (E.g., birthday, employment anniversary, etc.)

  • Does our PTO policy align with our company's mission, vision, and values?

  • How will we communicate our PTO policy to employees?

  • Is our PTO policy in compliance with local, state, and federal labor laws?



Sample PTO Policy

Purpose

[Company’s] PTO policy helps you achieve work-life balance and allows you to manage your time off according to your unique schedule and needs.

Eligibility

Full-time, three-quarter-time, and part-time employees are eligible to receive PTO benefits. Interns, temporary employees, and those working fewer than 20 hours per week are not eligible for PTO.

Accruing Paid Time Off

All employees accrue PTO at the same hourly rate; however, due to different work statuses,

total PTO accrued during a year will differ. During the first year of employment, PTO accrues

as follows:

  • Full-time employees accrue up to 15 full PTO days or 120 hours;

  • Three-quarter-time employees accrue up to 15 ¾ PTO days or 90 hours;

  • Part-time employees may accrue up to 15 ½ PTO days or 60 hours.

Full-time employees gain one additional day of PTO accrual each year during their first 5 years of tenure, reaching a maximum of 20 PTO days or 160 hours. Increases in PTO for

three-quarter-time and part-time employees occurs proportionately.

Additional Information:

  • Time-off hours accrue on the 1st and 16th of every month.

  • Annual PTO increases follow your anniversary date.

  • Unused PTO hours automatically roll over each year on January 1st.

    • Please note that an unused Floating Holiday and birthday time off expires at the end of the calendar year and doesn't roll over.

  • PTO never accrues beyond your current year maximum, regardless of how many

hours you roll over.

  • If you reach your PTO accrual maximum, accruals stop until PTO is taken.

  • Unused PTO is paid out upon termination of employment.


Accruing Floating Holidays

All employees receive four Floating Holidays each year, accruing one Floating Holiday at the beginning of each quarter. Due to different work statuses, total Floating Holidays accrued during the year will differ.

  • Full-time employees accrue up to four Floating Holiday days or 32 hours;

  • Three-quarter-time employees accrue up to three Floating Holiday days or 24 hours;

  • Part-time employees accrue up to two Floating Holiday days or 16 hours.

Additional Information:

  • Floating Holidays don't roll over to the next year.

  • Floating Holidays aren't eligible for pay-out upon termination of employment.

  • Certain leave of absence statuses may limit, suspend or disqualify you from additional PTO or Floating Holiday accruals. Please speak with HR if you are planning a leave of absence to understand how your benefits may be affected.

Managing Your PTO Hours

PTO includes all types of leave (vacation, sick time, personal days, emergencies, etc.). You are

responsible for managing your PTO, allowing adequate reserves for unplanned needs.

  • Always review your current and future PTO balance before requesting time off.

  • Approved time off may be adjusted or canceled if you use your available PTO in the

interim.

  • [Company] doesn't allow negative PTO balances (i.e. using PTO time that isn't

earned). If you are out of PTO and you'd like to take time away from work, you
should delay your time off until you have available PTO. If an emergency arises, please
speak with HR.

How Much Time Off Can I Take, and When?

When you’re planning time off, please consider the effect of your absence on [company], your team, and our clients.

Work with your manager to understand what coverage is needed during your absence. Coordinate PTO requests through your manager and with other team members.

  • PTO requests cannot exceed two consecutive weeks. Requests for time beyond two

weeks or back-to-back PTO requests are only permitted in case of emergencies or
special circumstances approved by your manager. (Note that in certain circumstances, it
may be necessary that your department head or division leader, as applicable, may need
to be consulted.)

  • PTO requests that overlap with the major company meetings will only be

approved in certain, special circumstances (e.g. family weddings and funerals, etc.).

  • Certain roles have blackout dates for time off. Please speak with your manager to

understand if blackout dates apply to your role or responsibilities.

Requesting Time-Off Approval

  • Planned PTO should be requested via [company HR software] at least one month before your leave.

  • Unplanned PTO (sickness, emergency, etc.) should be reported to managers as soon as

possible. Unplanned PTO must still be recorded in [company HR software].

  • State the reason for PTO in the request (vacation, sick, personal day, washing my dog,

PPV, etc.).

  • Time-off may be denied or canceled due to (but not limited to) the following reasons:

    • You don’t have enough PTO to cover the request.

    • The request didn’t meet the advanced notice needs of this Policy.

    • There's a blackout period during the requested time for your role.

    • Factors involving needs and fairness. Requests during the holidays or high

vacation periods may be denied to support proper team staffing or to
accommodate a rotation of other team members taking time off.

  • An emergency staffing or business need has arisen (e.g. ticket volume, busy

seasons for your role, team deadlines/goals, flu season crisis, etc.).

Rule of Thumb for Taking PTO

Over-communicate! Don't assume and avoid making non-refundable arrangements prior

to getting PTO approved.

Abstract / Introduction:

People trying to manage multiple financial accounts, a number of 401(k)s from past jobs, stock options, education funding needs, and figuring out how and when they might someday retire was complicated for most middle-income families. Seeking to address this issue, the purpose of this project is to create a better money management experience for consumers by blending cutting edge technology with objective financial advice. Wealth Warriors is a software and technology to give people insights, and to combine that with fiduciary advisors who would advise clients on how to plan and invest to meet their long-term goals and to lead users to a better financial life—meeting their long-term goals while reducing the stress and mystery surrounding personal finance.

Introduction:

Wealth Warriors is a financial platform that offers investment planning and wealth management tools. Wealth Warriors has a free and paid version: the free version comes with tools such as spending analysis, spending and saving analysis, portfolio performance, retirement progress and overall net worth.

Their retirement tool also makes it easy for users to plan for their retirement and experiment with different saving strategies.

The paid version of Wealth Warriors is for users who are willing to invest at least $100,000. The upgrade includes a team of advisors to help manage your wealth, and a starting fee of 0.89%.

If you invest more than $200,000, you get two financial advisors and a custom ETF portfolio. Users who invest more than $1 million get a fee as low as 0.49% and the ability to invest in individual bonds.

Functional Requirements:

  1. User management with authentication.

  2. User can choose between two subscription:

    1. Free

    2. Paid

  3. User can access different wealth management tools & Investment planning tools.

  4. User can do his/her spending analysis.

  5. User can do his/her saving analysis.

  6. User can view portfolio perfomance.

  7. User can view the retirement progress.

  8. User can view overall net worth.

Non-Functional Requirements:

  1. Security

  2. Reliability

  3. Availability

  4. Capacity, Growth & Scalability

  5. Response Time & Net Processing Time

  6. Target Audience & Communication

  7. Ongoing Support & Maintenance Requirements

  8. Maintainability

  9. System Management

  10. Legal / Regularity

  11. Ongoing Support & Maintenance Requirements

  12. Development Standards

  13. Up-To-Date Market Data

  14. Accurate Insights

Implementation:

Wealth warriors will be web-based and mobile app platforms (Apple, Android and Amazon), powered by market data delivered by Xignite. Xignite as a market data provider capable of delivering an affordable, easily integrated solution that is more aligned with the stature as a startup. Xignite is easy-to-integrate REST APIs, flexible volume-based pricing and accurate market data. We will select an array of Xignite Cloud APIs providing market data ranging from real-time and delayed quotes to historical pricing of stocks, mutual funds, ETFs, global equities, indices, and more. We need to plum the APIs into our backend databases and then serve them up to our web client via web services.

Introduction

Welcome to the Service Offering Development project page! This document serves as our central hub for all activities, strategies, and processes related to developing, launching, and optimizing our new service offerings. As we venture into expanding our services, it's crucial that we approach this project with creativity, customer-centricity, and strategic focus. Below you'll find detailed information on our project structure, key tasks, and how each team member can contribute.

Project Goals

  • Identify and Develop New Services: To conceptualize and introduce services that address unmet customer needs and market gaps.

  • Launch and Market New Offerings: To effectively launch these services, ensuring they reach our target audience with a compelling value proposition.

  • Optimize and Expand: To continuously refine our services based on customer feedback and expand our offerings in line with market trends and opportunities.

Project Structure

Section: Service Conceptualization

Our first phase focuses on ideating and validating new service opportunities, defining their scope, and setting clear objectives.

Tasks Overview:

  • Identify Service Opportunities: Dive deep into market analysis and customer feedback to spot potential service ideas.

  • Define Service Scope and Objectives: Outline what each service entails and the goals we aim to achieve.

Section: Service Design and Blueprinting

This section is dedicated to designing the blueprint of our services, prototyping, and initial testing.

Tasks Overview:

  • Create Service Blueprints: Detail the customer journey and operational requirements.

  • Prototype Service Delivery: Develop and refine our service prototypes based on real-world feedback.

Section: Pricing and Value Proposition

Here, we'll establish competitive pricing strategies and articulate compelling value propositions for our target audience.

Tasks Overview:

  • Develop Pricing Strategy: Set thoughtful pricing models that align with our service value and market standards.

  • Articulate Value Proposition: Define and communicate the unique benefits of our services.

Section: Launch and Marketing Strategy

The focus shifts to planning and executing a successful launch, accompanied by strategic marketing efforts.

Tasks Overview:

  • Plan Service Launch: Craft a comprehensive go-to-market plan.

  • Execute Marketing Campaign: Deploy marketing strategies to promote our new services effectively.

Section: Service Optimization and Expansion

Post-launch, our aim is to refine our offerings and explore avenues for expansion based on performance data and customer insights.

Tasks Overview:

  • Analyze Service Performance: Use data to guide our optimization efforts.

  • Expand Service Offerings: Continuously look for opportunities to grow and enhance our service portfolio.

Expectations from the Team

  • Collaboration: Engage actively with your teammates and cross-functional partners. Your insights and expertise are vital to our success.

  • Innovation: Think creatively and propose solutions that challenge the status quo.

  • Customer Focus: Always prioritize the needs and experiences of our customers in your work.

  • Agility: Be prepared to adapt to feedback and changes in the market. Our flexibility will be key to navigating the challenges ahead.

How to Contribute

  • Stay Informed: Regularly check this page for updates and new tasks.

  • Communicate: Share your progress, insights, and challenges openly. Utilize our communication platforms to stay connected.

  • Take Initiative: Don’t hesitate to take the lead on tasks that align with your skills and interests. Your proactive engagement is encouraged.

Conclusion

The Service Offering Development project represents a significant opportunity for us to grow and innovate. By working together with a shared vision and commitment, we can successfully develop and launch services that not only meet but exceed our customers' expectations.

Let's embark on this exciting journey together!

Service Offering Development Blueprint

Service Conceptualization

  • Identify Service Opportunities

    • Conduct market analysis to identify unmet needs.

    • Analyze customer feedback for service ideas.

    • Hold brainstorming sessions with the team for innovative service concepts.

  • Define Service Scope and Objectives

    • Draft service descriptions outlining key features and benefits.

    • Set measurable objectives for each service offering.

    • Validate service concepts with potential customers for preliminary feedback.

Service Design and Blueprinting

  • Create Service Blueprint

    • Map out the customer journey for each service offering.

    • Define the front stage (customer-facing) and backstage (operational) actions required to deliver the service.

    • Identify required resources, tools, and technologies for service delivery.

  • Prototype Service Delivery

    • Develop a prototype or pilot version of the service.

    • Conduct a small-scale test to test service delivery and gather feedback.

    • Refine the service based on pilot feedback.

Service Optimization and Expansion

  • Analyze Service Performance

    • Implement tools for tracking service usage, satisfaction, and feedback.

    • Regularly review service performance against objectives.

    • Identify areas for improvement or potential service enhancements.

  • Expand Service Offering

    • Explore opportunities for additional services or features based on market trends and customer feedback.

    • Validate new service ideas with customer research.

    • Plan and execute the development of new service expansions or enhancements.

Launch and Marketing Strategy

  • Plan Service Launch

    • Develop a comprehensive go-to-market strategy.

    • Schedule launch activities, including promotional events and marketing campaigns.

    • Prepare sales and support teams with training on new service offerings.

  • Execute Marketing Campaigns

    • Design and distribute marketing collateral across selected channels.

    • Monitor and adjust marketing efforts based on engagement and conversion metrics.

    • Collect and analyze customer feedback during the launch phase.

Pricing and Value Proposition

  • Develop Pricing Strategy

    • Analyze competitor pricing and value propositions.

    • Determine cost of service delivery and desired profit margins.

    • Set pricing tiers and models (subscription, one-time fee, etc.).

  • Articulate Value Proposition

    • Highlight unique benefits and differentiators of the service.

    • Develop key messaging for marketing and sales materials.

    • Validate value proposition with target customers for feedback.

Building a Customer 360° Knowledge Repository w/ Data Lake Explanation

Building a Customer 360° Knowledge Repository


What Is a Data Lake?

A data lake is a centralized repository that stores raw and structured data from various sources. It is designed to hold large volumes of data for analysis, reporting, and other business operations.

The diagram compares two approaches:

1.

Data Lake Without a 360° View: A traditional setup with siloed data, leading to inefficiencies.

2.

Data Lake With a 360° View: An advanced setup that integrates and connects data for faster and more comprehensive insights.

Challenges with a Data Lake Without a 360° View

  1. Delayed View of Customer State:

    • Insights about the customer’s current state are not readily available.

  2. Delays in Publishing to Purpose-Built Stores:

    • Siloed data sources make it time-consuming to build data stores for specific purposes.

  3. Time Spent on Data Discovery:

    • Analysts need to spend significant time correlating and understanding disconnected datasets.

How a Data Lake with a 360° View Solves These Challenges

By adding a Connected View, the data lake enables seamless integration and relationships between data sources, providing a unified view of the customer.

Key Enhancements in the 360° Data Lake Setup:

  1. Connected View:

    • Data is linked using tools like Amazon Neptune to establish relationships between datasets.

  2. Faster Access to Customer State:

    • Customer Service Representatives (CSRs) can quickly access the customer’s status without delays.

  3. Faster Data Discovery:

    • Analysts can use tools like Amazon SageMaker to discover and process data more efficiently.

  4. Streamlined Build of Purpose-Built Data Stores:

    • Connected data accelerates the creation of new data stores using platforms like Amazon Redshift and Amazon RDS.

Benefits of the 360° Data Lake

  1. Established Relationships for Traversal:

    • Data relationships allow better exploration and connections between datasets.

  2. Faster Insights:

    • Reduced time to access and analyze customer data.

  3. Enhanced Customer Experience:

    • Real-time data enables CSRs to respond quickly and accurately.

  4. Improved Data Discovery and Analysis:

    • Analysts can derive meaningful insights faster with connected datasets.

  5. Efficient Resource Utilization:

    • Integration reduces redundancy and ensures data consistency.

How the System Works

  • Data Sources:

    • Both external and internal data sources feed into the data lake.

  • Amazon S3:

    • Raw data is stored in the landing area and moved to a curated area for processing.

  • Amazon Neptune:

    • Creates a connected view of customer data by establishing relationships.

  • Purpose-Built Stores:

    • Tools like Amazon Redshift and Amazon RDS provide specific views for different use cases.

  • Data Analysis:

    • Platforms like Amazon SageMaker support advanced analytics, enabling deeper insights.

Conclusion

A 360° Data Lake transforms how organizations manage and leverage customer data. By integrating and connecting datasets, businesses can enhance customer experiences, streamline operations, and achieve faster, data-driven decision-making.

1. Understanding Key Business Insurance Types

• Cyber Insurance: Protects businesses against losses resulting from cyberattacks, data breaches, and other cyber-related incidents. Coverage typically includes costs associated with data recovery, legal fees, and notification expenses.

• Data Breach Insurance: Specifically focuses on covering expenses related to data breaches, including customer notification, credit monitoring services, and public relations efforts to manage the incident’s impact.

• Liability Insurance: A broad category that protects businesses from claims involving bodily injury, property damage, and other liabilities arising from business operations.

• Professional Liability Insurance: Also known as Errors and Omissions (E&O) insurance, it covers claims related to professional services provided, including negligence, misrepresentation, and inaccurate advice.

• General Liability Insurance: Protects against common business risks such as third-party bodily injury, property damage, and personal or advertising injury claims.

• Business Owner’s Policy (BOP): A bundled package that combines general liability insurance with commercial property insurance, often including business interruption coverage. It’s designed for small to medium-sized businesses to provide comprehensive protection.



2. Top Business Insurance Providers

Here are some reputable insurance companies offering various business insurance products:

• The Hartford: Offers a wide range of business insurance solutions, including general liability, professional liability, and BOPs.

• Hiscox: Specializes in small business insurance, providing tailored policies such as professional liability and general liability insurance.

• Chubb: Provides comprehensive business insurance options, including cyber insurance and BOPs, with a focus on larger small businesses.

• Nationwide: Offers general liability insurance and other business coverages, known for additional business services like retirement plans.

• Progressive: Known for commercial auto insurance, Progressive also offers various business insurance products suitable for different industries.

• State Farm: Provides a range of business insurance policies, including general liability and professional liability, with a strong customer satisfaction record.



3. Steps to Obtain Business Insurance

  1. Assess Your Business Risks: Identify potential risks associated with your industry and operations to determine the necessary coverage types.

  2. Research Insurance Providers: Compare offerings from various insurers to find policies that align with your business needs and budget.

  3. Obtain Quotes: Request quotes from multiple providers to compare coverage options and premiums.

  4. Review Policy Details: Carefully examine policy terms, coverage limits, exclusions, and deductibles.

  5. Consult an Insurance Agent: Seek professional advice to ensure you select appropriate coverage tailored to your business.

  6. Purchase and Maintain Coverage: Once selected, purchase the policy and regularly review it to ensure it continues to meet your business’s evolving needs.

4. Additional Resources

• Small Business Administration (SBA): Offers guidance on business insurance and risk management.

• Investopedia: Provides detailed articles on various types of business insurance and their importance.

• NerdWallet: Features comparisons of top business insurance providers and tips for selecting the right coverage.

By understanding these insurance types and following the outlined steps, you can effectively protect your business from potential risks and liabilities.

Competitive Marketing Strategy



Market and Competitor Analysis

1. Research market trends and customer preferences.

2. Identify market gaps and opportunities.

3. Analyze competitor marketing strategies and positioning.

4. Compile a competitor feature and pricing comparison.

Strategy Development

1. Segment the market based on demographic, psychographic, and behavioral data.

2. Create detailed buyer personas.

3. Set specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) marketing goals.

4. Align marketing objectives with overall business targets.

Multi-Channel Marketing Plan

1. Develop a content calendar outlining topics, formats, and publishing schedules.

2. Determine content creation resources and responsibilities.

3. Evaluate the effectiveness of various channels (social media, email, SEO, etc.).

4. Choose channels based on target audience preferences and marketing goals.

Implementation and Execution

1. Execute marketing campaigns across selected channels.

2. Monitor campaign performance and adjust strategies as needed.

3. Ensure sales team is informed about marketing campaigns and provided with necessary materials.

4. Set up a system for lead sharing and feedback between sales and marketing.

Measurement and Optimization

1. Identify key performance indicators (KPIs) for each marketing channel and campaign.

2. Implement tools for tracking and analysis.

3. Regularly review campaign data to assess performance against KPIs.

4. Conduct A/B testing to optimize marketing messages and channels.

5. Gather insights from campaign performance and market feedback.
